metrics.name: assertion_pass_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of pre-registered assertions that pass for a given run. Prefer skill-creator's agents/grader.md when reachable (primary); otherwise use this skill's own agents/grader.md (fallback) -- same ordering as SKILL.md Step 3 and references/skill-creator-integration.md. Do NOT load both.

metrics.name: l0_skill_quality_score
metrics.description: 8-dimension, 990-point rubric (D1-D8, quality axis) scoring the target skill's own SKILL.md design quality, plus a separate 1-5 Eval-Design Checks trio: instruction clarity and test prompt realism (quality axis), and description accuracy -- references/layers-and-metrics.md's L0 Correctness axis ('is the description factually accurate about what the skill does?'), which is why this entry is tagged with both axes, not quality alone. L0 only — see rubric_quality_score below for L1/L2.

metrics.name: rubric_quality_score
metrics.description: 1-5 blind rubric score per dimension for output-level quality assertions can't capture (clarity, tone, judgment). Prefer an adapted skill-creator quality judge when reachable; otherwise agents/generic-quality-judge.md -- it doesn't carry a fixed rubric, it defines the discipline for pre-registering one into eval_plan.json's scope.quality_rubric before any output exists. Routing rule: use manual_tc_quality_score (below) whenever the skill under test writes manual test cases; use this entry for every other skill type instead — never both for the same run. NOT agents/input-layer-judge.md (L0-only, 990-point scale) and NOT agents/manual-tc-quality-judge.md (that's manual_tc_quality_score's scorer, not this one).

metrics.name: manual_tc_quality_score
metrics.description: Blind rubric score (1-5 per dimension) for manual test-case craftsmanship: traceability, atomicity, clarity/reproducibility, coverage, expected-result precision. Use for skills whose job is writing manual test cases — for every other skill type, use rubric_quality_score (above) instead; correctness/format is graded separately by assertions via agents/grader.md.

metrics.name: token_efficiency
metrics.description: Mean tokens consumed per run, with stddev across repeats.

metrics.name: time_efficiency
metrics.description: Mean wall-clock duration per run, with stddev across repeats.

metrics.name: tool_call_efficiency
metrics.description: Mean tool_calls per run, with stddev across repeats -- captured per SKILL.md Step 3 ('Capture tokens/time/tool-calls per run'), aggregated into `efficiency_tool_calls` alongside token_efficiency and time_efficiency.

metrics.name: run_variance
metrics.description: Stddev of correctness/quality/efficiency across N repeats of the same prompt+configuration.

metrics.name: refinement_delta
metrics.description: L2-minus-L1 comparison: which assertions flipped, where quality changed and why, substance-vs-polish judgment, cost/benefit verdict.

metrics.name: version_ab_delta
metrics.description: Blind A/B comparison between two configurations at the same layer (e.g. skill v1 vs v2, or with_skill vs without_skill) — distinct from refinement_delta, which compares L1 vs L2 within one configuration, not across versions. scorer_type is 'rubric', not 'derived', because agents/comparator.md performs a fresh blind grading pass on both sides itself (it does not receive already-scored results the way agents/refinement-analyzer.md does). Prefer skill-creator's agents/comparator.md + agents/analyzer.md when reachable; otherwise use this skill's own agents/comparator.md (fallback).

_extend_by: Append a new object with name/axis/applies_to_layers/scorer_type/scorer_ref/description. `axis` is always an array, even for a single-axis metric (e.g. ["correctness"]) -- a metric spanning multiple axes (e.g. refinement_delta) lists them all as separate array entries, never a comma-joined string. scorer_type is one of: assertion (script-checkable), rubric (needs a blind judge prompt), derived (computed from other metrics' already-recorded data). No changes to SKILL.md's workflow steps are needed to pick up a new metric -- only the scorer implementation and this registry entry.
